en: to worry, to fret; to be troubled, to torment oneself
usage: Literary and slightly old-fashioned for a gnawing, persistent worry ('il cruccio'), gentler than 'tormentarsi' and more inward than 'preoccuparsi'. Often heard in the negative imperative 'non crucciarti'. Regular -are verb (mi cruccio, ti crucci); the transitive 'cruciare' is archaic.

examples.it: Si cruccia da mesi per la salute della madre.
examples.en: She has been fretting for months over her mother's health.

examples.it: Non crucciarti: sarà quel che sarà.
examples.en: Don't torment yourself: what will be, will be.

examples.it: Si era crucciato a lungo di non aver detto addio al padre.
examples.en: He had long been troubled that he had not said goodbye to his father.

en: to extol, to sing the praises of; (chemistry, wine) to decant, to let settle
usage: Two unrelated verbs: from 'cantare', to praise loudly and at length, often with irony ('le tanto decantate riforme'); from the Latin 'decanthare', to let a liquid settle or, figuratively, to let a situation or an idea settle ('lasciamo decantare la polemica'). Regular -are verb; in the settling sense it is intransitive and takes essere or avere.

examples.it: I giornali decantavano le virtù del nuovo sindaco.
examples.en: The newspapers were extolling the virtues of the new mayor.

examples.it: Ho lasciato decantare il vino per un'ora prima di servirlo.
examples.en: I let the wine breathe for an hour before serving it.

examples.it: Prima di rispondere, lascia che la rabbia decanti.
examples.en: Before answering, let your anger settle.

en: to oust, to dismiss abruptly (from office); (literally) to throw out of a window
usage: From the Defenestration of Prague: today almost always figurative and journalistic, for the brutal removal of a manager, coach or politician ('il presidente è stato defenestrato dal consiglio'). Stronger and more colourful than 'destituire' or 'silurare' (colloquial). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: L'allenatore fu defenestrato dopo tre sconfitte consecutive.
examples.en: The coach was ousted after three consecutive defeats.

examples.it: Temono che il nuovo azionista defenestri l'intero vertice aziendale.
examples.en: They fear the new shareholder will oust the entire top management.

examples.it: Nel 1618 i ribelli boemi defenestrarono i governatori imperiali.
examples.en: In 1618 the Bohemian rebels threw the imperial governors out of the window.

en: to deflagrate, to burst into flames; to explode (also figuratively)
usage: Technical term of chemistry and ballistics (rapid combustion without the shock wave of a 'detonazione'), widely used by journalists for crises that suddenly flare up ('la protesta è deflagrata in tutto il paese'). Regular -are verb; auxiliary essere or, less often, avere.

examples.it: La miscela di gas deflagrò distruggendo il laboratorio.
examples.en: The gas mixture deflagrated, destroying the laboratory.

examples.it: La crisi è deflagrata proprio alla vigilia delle elezioni.
examples.en: The crisis erupted right on the eve of the elections.

examples.it: Una scintilla basterebbe a far deflagrare il conflitto.
examples.en: A single spark would be enough to make the conflict explode.

en: to delight; (deliziarsi) to take delight in
usage: Elegant and often playful: to give someone exquisite pleasure, typically with food, music or wit ('ci ha deliziato con un risotto'). The pronominal 'deliziarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to savour something with relish. Regular -are verb (delizio, delizi).

examples.it: Il pianista deliziò il pubblico con un bis inaspettato.
examples.en: The pianist delighted the audience with an unexpected encore.

examples.it: Ci deliziammo a guardare il tramonto dalla terrazza.
examples.en: We took delight in watching the sunset from the terrace.

examples.it: Spero che il dolce vi abbia deliziati.
examples.en: I hope the dessert delighted you.

en: to cross out, to strike off (a list)
usage: Bureaucratic-formal: to strike a name or item off a list or register ('depennare dall'elenco dei fornitori'), literally with a stroke of the pen. Everyday speech prefers 'cancellare'; 'espungere' is the philological cousin. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il suo nome è stato depennato dalla lista degli invitati.
examples.en: His name has been struck off the guest list.

examples.it: Depennarono una a una tutte le voci di spesa superflue.
examples.en: They crossed out one by one all the superfluous items of expenditure.

examples.it: Se non paghi la quota, ti depenneranno dall'albo.
examples.en: If you don't pay the fee, they'll strike you off the register.

en: to derail, to go off the rails (also figuratively)
usage: Technical railway term (from the French 'dérailler'), used figuratively for conversations, negotiations or lives that go off track ('il dibattito è deragliato'). Regular -are verb; auxiliary essere in careful usage, avere also accepted. The causative is 'far deragliare'.

examples.it: Il treno merci è deragliato poco prima della stazione.
examples.en: The goods train derailed just before the station.

examples.it: Non lasciare che la discussione deragli sulle solite polemiche.
examples.en: Don't let the discussion go off the rails onto the usual squabbles.

examples.it: Una frana fece deragliare il convoglio.
examples.en: A landslide derailed the train.

en: to derogate from, to make an exception to (a rule)
usage: Juridical verb governing 'a': a later or special rule 'deroga' to a general one, and an authority may 'derogare' to a requirement in specific cases. The noun 'deroga' ('in deroga a', by way of exception to) is extremely common in administrative language. Regular -are verb with -ghi/-ghe spelling (deroghi).

examples.it: Il regolamento comunale non può derogare alla legge nazionale.
examples.en: The municipal regulation cannot derogate from national law.

examples.it: In casi eccezionali il rettore può derogare ai requisiti di ammissione.
examples.en: In exceptional cases the rector may waive the admission requirements.

examples.it: Non credo che il tribunale abbia derogato ai propri criteri abituali.
examples.en: I don't think the court departed from its usual criteria.

en: to desist; to give up, to cease
usage: Formal-juridical verb governing 'da': 'desistere dal proposito', 'desistere dall'azione' (in criminal law 'desistenza volontaria' is voluntary abandonment of an attempted crime). Everyday speech says 'rinunciare' or 'smettere'. Regular like the other -sistere verbs: participle 'desistito', passato remoto 'desistetti' or 'desistei'; auxiliary avere.

examples.it: Nonostante le minacce, il giornalista non desistette dall'inchiesta.
examples.en: Despite the threats, the journalist did not give up his investigation.

examples.it: Vi invitiamo a desistere da ogni ulteriore tentativo di contatto.
examples.en: We ask you to desist from any further attempt at contact.

examples.it: Se avesse desistito prima, avrebbe evitato la condanna.
examples.en: Had he desisted earlier, he would have avoided conviction.

en: to deduct; to subtract
usage: Fiscal and accounting verb: to deduct an amount from a sum, above all from taxes ('detrarre le spese mediche', 'detrazione fiscale'); technically distinct from 'dedurre' (deduct from taxable income) in Italian tax law. Irregular like 'trarre': detraggo, detrassi, detratto, detrarrò.

examples.it: Puoi detrarre il 19 per cento delle spese sanitarie.
examples.en: You can deduct 19 percent of your medical expenses.

examples.it: Dall'importo vanno detratte le somme già versate.
examples.en: The sums already paid must be deducted from the amount.

examples.it: Detrassero dallo stipendio i giorni di assenza ingiustificata.
examples.en: They deducted the days of unjustified absence from his salary.

en: to tear to pieces, to rend; to torment
usage: Literary and journalistic: literally of wild beasts tearing flesh, figuratively of grief, remorse or factional strife ('un partito dilaniato dalle correnti'). Stronger than 'lacerare' and 'straziare'; the pronominal 'dilaniarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to tear one another apart. Regular -are verb (dilanio, dilani).

examples.it: Le belve dilaniarono la carcassa in pochi minuti.
examples.en: The beasts tore the carcass to pieces in a few minutes.

examples.it: Il rimorso lo dilaniava giorno e notte.
examples.en: Remorse tormented him day and night.

examples.it: Il paese è dilaniato da una guerra civile che dura da anni.
examples.en: The country is torn apart by a civil war that has been going on for years.

en: to vanish, to melt away; to slip away
usage: Elegant verb for disappearing gradually or unnoticed: mist, sounds, hopes and, colloquially, people who slip away without paying ('si è dileguato con la cassa'). Compare 'svanire' (to fade) and 'sparire' (neutral, sudden). Regular -are verb; the transitive 'dileguare' is literary.

examples.it: La nebbia si dileguò con i primi raggi del sole.
examples.en: The mist melted away with the first rays of the sun.

examples.it: I ladri si sono dileguati prima dell'arrivo della polizia.
examples.en: The thieves vanished before the police arrived.

examples.it: Ogni speranza si dileguerebbe, se lui non tornasse.
examples.en: All hope would vanish, if he did not return.

en: to wag, to wave about, to shake; (dimenarsi) to thrash about, to wriggle
usage: To move part of the body back and forth with energy: a dog 'dimena la coda', a dancer 'dimena i fianchi'; the pronominal 'dimenarsi' (auxiliary essere) is to thrash about, also figuratively to struggle ('dimenarsi tra mille impegni'). Colloquial-descriptive; 'agitare' is the neutral verb. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il cane dimenava la coda festoso.
examples.en: The dog was wagging its tail joyfully.

examples.it: Il pesce si dimenò sulla banchina finché non lo ributtarono in acqua.
examples.en: The fish thrashed about on the pier until they threw it back into the water.

examples.it: Smetti di dimenarti e stai fermo mentre ti pettino.
examples.en: Stop wriggling and keep still while I comb your hair.

en: to unravel, to disentangle; to sort out (a problem)
usage: From winding yarn off a skein: to disentangle an intricate matter ('dipanare la matassa', to sort out the tangle). The pronominal 'dipanarsi' (auxiliary essere) describes a plot or a road unfolding. More literary than 'sbrogliare' and 'districare'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ci vorranno mesi per dipanare l'intreccio di società offshore.
examples.en: It will take months to unravel the web of offshore companies.

examples.it: La trama si dipana lentamente, tra flashback e digressioni.
examples.en: The plot unfolds slowly, between flashbacks and digressions.

examples.it: Se avessimo dipanato subito il malinteso, non saremmo qui a litigare.
examples.en: If we had cleared up the misunderstanding right away, we wouldn't be here arguing.

en: to discourse at length (learnedly or pedantically)
usage: To discuss a subject in a learned, subtle and often pedantic way ('disquisire di massimi sistemi'); the noun 'disquisizione' is frequently ironic ('lunghe disquisizioni filosofiche'). Conjugated with -isc- (disquisisco); governs 'di', 'su' or 'intorno a'.

examples.it: Disquisirono per ore sul sesso degli angeli mentre la casa bruciava.
examples.en: They discoursed for hours on the sex of angels while the house burned.

examples.it: Non è il momento di disquisire di filosofia del diritto.
examples.en: This is not the time to hold forth on the philosophy of law.

examples.it: Che disquisisca pure di etica: i fatti parlano da soli.
examples.en: Let him hold forth on ethics: the facts speak for themselves.

en: to break up (uncultivated ground), to till for the first time; to clear (land)
usage: Agricultural term for turning over hard, uncultivated soil to make it arable; figuratively, to prepare the ground for a new field of study ('dissodare un terreno di ricerca'). 'Arare' is routine ploughing, 'dissodare' the first, hard breaking of the sod. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: I coloni dissodarono la brughiera e vi piantarono grano.
examples.en: The settlers broke up the heath and planted wheat there.

examples.it: Bisognerà dissodare il campo prima che arrivino le piogge.
examples.en: The field will have to be broken up before the rains come.

examples.it: Quei primi studiosi hanno dissodato un terreno che altri avrebbero coltivato.
examples.en: Those first scholars broke ground that others would go on to cultivate.

en: to sweeten; to water down, to sugar-coat
usage: Literally a pharmaceutical term (to add sweetener), almost always figurative today: to soften a harsh truth or an account ('una versione edulcorata dei fatti'). Journalistic-critical register; 'addolcire' is neutral, 'edulcorare' implies disapproval of the concealment. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Il film edulcora la biografia del protagonista fino a renderla irriconoscibile.
examples.en: The film sugar-coats the protagonist's life story to the point of making it unrecognisable.

examples.it: Non edulcorate la diagnosi: vogliamo sapere la verità.
examples.en: Don't water down the diagnosis: we want to know the truth.

examples.it: Ci hanno raccontato una storia edulcorata, ma la realtà era ben più cruda.
examples.en: They told us a sanitised story, but the reality was far harsher.

en: to pour out, to give vent to (feelings); (effondersi) to spread, to overflow
usage: Aulic Latinism for pouring out feelings, light or fragrance; today survives mainly in the pronominal 'effondersi in' (to launch into effusive expressions: 'effondersi in ringraziamenti', auxiliary essere) and in the noun 'effusione'. Irregular like 'fondere': effusi, effuso.

examples.it: Il poeta effondeva nei versi tutto il suo dolore.
examples.en: The poet poured all his grief into his verses.

examples.it: Si effuse in lodi sperticate verso il nuovo direttore.
examples.en: He launched into extravagant praise of the new director.

examples.it: Un profumo di gelsomino si era effuso per tutto il giardino.
examples.en: A scent of jasmine had spread throughout the garden.

en: to bestow generously; to lavish; to grant
usage: Formal verb for giving generously from a position of abundance or power ('elargire contributi, premi, favori'); often ironic when applied to advice or promises ('elargire consigli non richiesti'). 'Donare' is neutral, 'dispensare' more mechanical. Conjugated with -isc- (elargisco).

examples.it: La fondazione elargisce ogni anno borse di studio a studenti meritevoli.
examples.en: Every year the foundation awards scholarships to deserving students.

examples.it: Il sovrano elargì titoli e terre ai suoi fedeli.
examples.en: The sovereign bestowed titles and lands on his loyal followers.

examples.it: Vorrei che smettesse di elargire consigli che nessuno gli ha chiesto.
examples.en: I wish he would stop dispensing advice nobody asked him for.

en: to cogitate laboriously; to concoct (theories) by long brooding
usage: Learned and mostly ironic (from 'lucubrare', to work by lamplight): to produce ideas through long and tortuous mental effort; the noun 'elucubrazione' is almost always spregiativo ('le sue elucubrazioni'). Regular -are verb (elùcubro).

examples.it: Passò la notte a elucubrare un piano per riconquistarla.
examples.en: He spent the night cogitating a plan to win her back.

examples.it: Invece di elucubrare teorie, prova a parlare con lei.
examples.en: Instead of concocting theories, try talking to her.

examples.it: Cosa avrà elucubrato questa volta la nostra commissione?
examples.en: What will our committee have dreamt up this time?

en: to amend (a law, a text); to correct; (emendarsi) to mend one's ways
usage: Parliamentary and philological verb: to amend a bill ('emendare un disegno di legge') or to correct a corrupt text; the moral sense 'emendarsi' (auxiliary essere) is literary. The noun 'emendamento' is everyday political vocabulary. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La commissione ha emendato l'articolo 5 in più punti.
examples.en: The committee amended Article 5 in several places.

examples.it: Il filologo emendò il passo corrotto ricorrendo a un manoscritto più antico.
examples.en: The philologist corrected the corrupt passage by resorting to an older manuscript.

examples.it: Chi si emenda dei propri errori merita una seconda possibilità.
examples.en: Whoever mends their ways deserves a second chance.

en: to burst out, to erupt; to break out (into laughter, tears)
usage: Literary verb for a sudden violent outburst: lava from a volcano, water from a breach, a cry or laughter from a person ('erompere in singhiozzi'). 'Prorompere' is the closer synonym, 'scoppiare' the everyday one. Irregular like 'rompere': eruppe, erotto (participle rare); auxiliary essere.

examples.it: Dalla folla eruppe un grido di gioia.
examples.en: A cry of joy burst from the crowd.

examples.it: La lava erompeva dal cratere illuminando la notte.
examples.en: Lava was erupting from the crater, lighting up the night.

examples.it: Temevo che sarebbe erotta in lacrime davanti a tutti.
examples.en: I feared she would burst into tears in front of everyone.

en: to exacerbate; to embitter; to aggravate
usage: Learned verb for making a conflict, a pain or a mood harsher ('esacerbare gli animi', 'esacerbare le tensioni'); the pronominal 'esacerbarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to become embittered or worse. Compare 'inasprire' (neutral-formal) and 'acuire'. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Le dichiarazioni del ministro hanno esacerbato gli animi.
examples.en: The minister's statements inflamed people's feelings.

examples.it: Il dolore si esacerbò durante la notte.
examples.en: The pain grew worse during the night.

examples.it: Temo che una nuova tassa esacerbi il malcontento popolare.
examples.en: I fear that a new tax will exacerbate popular discontent.

en: to execrate, to loathe; to condemn with horror
usage: Solemn, almost religious verb for detesting and cursing something as abominable; used in high moral and political prose ('un crimine esecrato da tutti'). Stronger than 'detestare' and 'aborrire'. Regular -are verb: 'esècro' (stress on the second e); the adjective 'esecrabile' is more common than the verb.

examples.it: Tutti esecrano quel massacro, ma pochi ne parlano.
examples.en: Everyone abhors that massacre, but few speak of it.

examples.it: I contemporanei esecrarono il tiranno che i posteri avrebbero riabilitato.
examples.en: His contemporaries execrated the tyrant whom posterity would rehabilitate.

examples.it: Non basta che si esecri la violenza a parole.
examples.en: It is not enough to condemn violence in words.

en: to expunge, to delete (from a text or list)
patterns: espungere un passo da un testo
usage: Philological and juridical verb: to remove a word, passage or clause considered spurious or inadmissible ('espungere una clausola dal contratto'). Everyday speech says 'togliere' or 'cancellare'; 'depennare' is its bureaucratic cousin. Irregular like 'pungere': espunsi, espunto.

examples.it: L'editore espunse dal testo le interpolazioni più evidenti.
examples.en: The editor expunged the most obvious interpolations from the text.

examples.it: Il giudice ha espunto dal fascicolo le intercettazioni irrilevanti.
examples.en: The judge removed the irrelevant wiretaps from the case file.

examples.it: Vorrei che quel paragrafo fosse espunto dalla versione definitiva.
examples.en: I would like that paragraph to be deleted from the final version.

en: to extort; to wring (a confession, a promise) out of someone
usage: Juridical and journalistic: to obtain money or a statement by threat, violence or pressure ('estorcere una confessione con la tortura'); the crime is 'estorsione'. Irregular like 'torcere': estorsi, estorto. Note the indirect object with 'a' for the victim.

examples.it: La banda estorceva denaro ai commercianti del quartiere.
examples.en: The gang extorted money from the neighbourhood shopkeepers.

examples.it: Gli estorsero una confessione dopo dodici ore di interrogatorio.
examples.en: They wrung a confession out of him after twelve hours of questioning.

examples.it: Una promessa estorta con il ricatto non vale nulla.
examples.en: A promise extorted by blackmail is worth nothing.

en: to express outwardly, to manifest; (estrinsecarsi) to take concrete form
usage: Philosophical and bureaucratic Latinism: to bring an inner quality or intention into external form ('estrinsecare il proprio pensiero'); the pronominal 'estrinsecarsi in' (auxiliary essere) is common in official prose ('l'attività si estrinseca in tre fasi'). 'Manifestare' or 'esprimere' are the plain alternatives. Regular -are verb (estrinsechi).

examples.it: La sua ostilità si estrinsecava in piccoli dispetti quotidiani.
examples.en: His hostility manifested itself in small daily spites.

examples.it: L'artista estrinsecò nel colore ciò che non riusciva a dire a parole.
examples.en: The artist expressed in colour what he could not say in words.

examples.it: Vorremmo che il vostro impegno si estrinsecasse in atti concreti.
examples.en: We would like your commitment to take the form of concrete acts.

en: to infer, to deduce (from evidence)
usage: Juridical-bureaucratic verb used almost exclusively in the impersonal 'si evince' ('come si evince dai documenti', as the documents show). Irregular like 'vincere': evinsi, evinto (rarely used). In ordinary prose 'dedurre' or 'risultare' are preferable; using 'evincere' actively ('ho evinto che') sounds stilted.

examples.it: Dalla perizia si evince che l'incidente era inevitabile.
examples.en: It can be inferred from the expert report that the accident was unavoidable.

examples.it: Come si evinceva dal bilancio, l'azienda era già in perdita.
examples.en: As could be deduced from the balance sheet, the company was already making a loss.

examples.it: Non si evince con chiarezza chi abbia autorizzato il pagamento.
examples.en: It is not clear who authorised the payment.

en: to rave; to talk deliriously, to talk nonsense
usage: Literally to be delirious with fever; figuratively, and strongly spregiativo, to spout absurd ideas ('farnetica di complotti'). 'Delirare' is medical or emphatic, 'vaneggiare' more literary, 'farneticare' the harsher everyday judgement. Regular -are verb (farnetichi); the noun is 'farneticazione'.

examples.it: Il malato farneticava e chiamava persone morte da anni.
examples.en: The patient was raving and calling out to people long dead.

examples.it: Che cosa farnetichi? Nessuno vuole licenziarti.
examples.en: What are you raving about? Nobody wants to fire you.

examples.it: Chiunque lo ascolti per cinque minuti capisce che farnetica.
examples.en: Anyone who listens to him for five minutes realises he's talking nonsense.

en: to cleave, to split; to cut through (water, a crowd)
usage: Literary verb for splitting with a sharp blow or cutting through a medium: 'fendere l'aria', 'la prua fende le onde', 'un grido fendette il silenzio'. The pronominal 'fendersi' means to crack open. Passato remoto 'fendei' or 'fendetti'; the participle is 'fenduto', with the archaic 'fesso' surviving only as an adjective (also colloquially 'fool').

examples.it: La nave fendeva le onde a tutta velocità.
examples.en: The ship was cutting through the waves at full speed.

examples.it: Un urlo fendette il silenzio della notte.
examples.en: A scream rent the silence of the night.

examples.it: Il terremoto ha fenduto la parete della chiesa dal tetto al pavimento.
examples.en: The earthquake has split the church wall from roof to floor.

en: to fund, to bankroll (often covertly); to supply with fodder
usage: From 'foraggio' (fodder): originally to feed horses, today almost always journalistic and spregiativo for financing a party, newspaper or clientele to buy its loyalty ('foraggiare la stampa amica'). 'Finanziare' is neutral, 'sovvenzionare' formal. Regular -are verb (foraggio, foraggi).

examples.it: Per anni il regime ha foraggiato i giornali compiacenti.
examples.en: For years the regime bankrolled the compliant newspapers.

examples.it: Si sospetta che quella fondazione foraggi gruppi estremisti.
examples.en: That foundation is suspected of funding extremist groups.

examples.it: Chi avrà foraggiato una campagna elettorale così costosa?
examples.en: Who can have bankrolled such an expensive election campaign?

en: to break, to shatter; (frangersi) to break (of waves)
usage: Literary verb (Dante, Leopardi) that in modern Italian survives chiefly in the pronominal 'frangersi' for waves breaking on rocks (auxiliary essere) and in derivatives ('frangiflutti', 'infrangere', 'frantoio'). Irregular: fransi, franto; the transitive sense also covers crushing olives.

examples.it: Le onde si frangevano con fragore contro la scogliera.
examples.en: The waves were breaking noisily against the cliff.

examples.it: Nel frantoio le olive vengono frante entro poche ore dalla raccolta.
examples.en: In the mill the olives are crushed within a few hours of harvesting.

examples.it: Ogni sua speranza si franse contro l'indifferenza dei giudici.
examples.en: All his hopes were shattered against the indifference of the judges.

en: to chirp, to twitter (of swallows); to flutter (of flags)
usage: Poetic verb (Pascoli, D'Annunzio) for the shrill cry of swallows and, by extension, for banners snapping in the wind ('bandiere che garriscono al vento'). Conjugated with -isc- (garrisce); used almost only in the third person. 'Cinguettare' is the everyday verb for birdsong.

examples.it: Le rondini garrivano intorno al campanile.
examples.en: The swallows were twittering around the bell tower.

examples.it: Sulla torre garriva la bandiera della repubblica.
examples.en: On the tower the flag of the republic fluttered in the wind.

examples.it: Che le rondini garriscano ancora sotto quel tetto è un buon segno.
examples.en: That swallows still chirp under that roof is a good sign.

en: to seize with claws, to snatch; to grab suddenly
usage: Literary verb for a bird of prey or beast seizing its victim, extended to sudden violent grabbing by people or by death and illness ('la morte lo ghermì nel sonno'). Conjugated with -isc- (ghermisco); 'afferrare' is the neutral equivalent, 'artigliare' the closest synonym.

examples.it: Il falco ghermì la lepre e si alzò in volo.
examples.en: The hawk seized the hare and rose into the air.

examples.it: Una mano lo ghermì per il colletto e lo trascinò indietro.
examples.en: A hand grabbed him by the collar and dragged him back.

examples.it: Temo che la febbre lo abbia ghermito proprio alla vigilia della partenza.
examples.en: I fear the fever seized him right on the eve of his departure.

en: to gloat; to be overjoyed, to beam with satisfaction
usage: Familiar and picturesque: to show open, slightly smug delight ('gongolava per la promozione'), often with the undertone of gloating over a rival's misfortune. 'Esultare' is the neutral verb for rejoicing; 'gongolare' adds the visible glow of self-satisfaction. Regular -are verb (góngolo).

examples.it: Gongolava come un bambino davanti ai complimenti.
examples.en: He was beaming like a child at the compliments.

examples.it: I tifosi gongolarono per tutta la settimana dopo il derby.
examples.en: The fans gloated all week after the derby.

examples.it: Non gongolare troppo: la rivincita è tra un mese.
examples.en: Don't gloat too much: the rematch is in a month.

en: to fill to overflowing, to pack; (gremirsi) to fill up (with people)
usage: Journalistic-literary verb for crowds filling a place completely ('una folla gremiva la piazza'); the participle 'gremito' ('teatro gremito in ogni ordine di posti') is the most common form, and 'gremirsi' (auxiliary essere) means to fill up. Conjugated with -isc- (gremisce). 'Riempire' is neutral; 'affollare' close but less intense.

examples.it: Una folla immensa gremiva la basilica.
examples.en: An immense crowd packed the basilica.

examples.it: Lo stadio si gremì un'ora prima del fischio d'inizio.
examples.en: The stadium filled up an hour before kick-off.

examples.it: Spero che la sala si gremisca anche per la replica.
examples.en: I hope the hall will be packed for the second performance too.

en: to hawk, to tout; to win over with glib talk
usage: From the street-market 'imbonitore' (barker): to attract and soften up an audience or a customer with a torrent of persuasive patter; spregiativo when applied to politicians or salesmen. Conjugated with -isc- (imbonisco). 'Lusingare' flatters, 'imbonire' sells.

examples.it: Il venditore imboniva i passanti con promesse mirabolanti.
examples.en: The seller was hawking to passers-by with amazing promises.

examples.it: Non farti imbonire da chi promette rendimenti garantiti.
examples.en: Don't let yourself be sweet-talked by anyone promising guaranteed returns.

examples.it: Imbonì la platea per venti minuti prima di arrivare al dunque.
examples.en: He softened up the audience for twenty minutes before getting to the point.

en: to rage (of storms, epidemics, wars); to be rampant, to be all the rage
usage: Said of violent phenomena raging unchecked: 'la tempesta imperversava', 'imperversa l'epidemia'; ironically, of fashions or people who are everywhere ('quest'estate imperversa il reggaeton', 'il comico imperversa in tv'). Journalistic-literary; 'infuriare' is the near synonym for storms. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: La bufera imperversò per tre giorni sulla costa.
examples.en: The storm raged for three days along the coast.

examples.it: Mentre la peste imperversava, i signori fuggivano in campagna.
examples.en: While the plague raged, the lords fled to the countryside.

examples.it: Sui social imperversa da settimane la polemica sul nuovo stadio.
examples.en: On social media the row over the new stadium has been raging for weeks.

en: to fatten; to swell (coffers, a bank account); (impinguarsi) to grow fat, to enrich oneself
usage: From 'pingue' (fat): literally to fatten animals, figuratively and often ironically to swell coffers, files or bank accounts ('impinguare il bilancio con nuove tasse'). The pronominal 'impinguarsi' (auxiliary essere) means to get fat or rich at others' expense. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Le multe servivano solo a impinguare le casse del comune.
examples.en: The fines served only to swell the municipality's coffers.

examples.it: Qualcuno si è impinguato con i fondi destinati alla ricostruzione.
examples.en: Somebody grew rich on the funds intended for reconstruction.

examples.it: Temo che il nuovo capitolo impingui il volume senza arricchirlo.
examples.en: I fear the new chapter pads the volume without enriching it.

en: to advance with solemn, stately steps; to stride majestically
usage: Aulic verb for a slow, dignified, ceremonial walk ('incedere maestoso'), used also as a noun ('l'incedere della processione', 'l'incedere del tempo'). Defective: used practically only in the present, imperfect and gerund, with no participle in common use (passato remoto 'incedette' is very rare). Often ironic when applied to pompous people.

examples.it: La regina incedeva lentamente lungo la navata.
examples.en: The queen advanced slowly along the nave.

examples.it: Incede come se il corridoio dell'ufficio fosse una passerella.
examples.en: He struts along as if the office corridor were a catwalk.

examples.it: Incedendo con solennità, i cardinali entrarono nella cappella.
examples.en: Advancing solemnly, the cardinals entered the chapel.
